title: Make the Flowershow site read as one coherent guide
description:
New-thread task. Problem (Rufus 2026-10-05): the published site reads worse than the one-page guide.html, especially for designers: README opens with maintainer notes (where it's published, python rebuild commands), the home is a list of links, and the left sidebar lists every file and overwhelms. Recommended approach (check with Rufus first, propose before changing):
1. Home = a designed page: either guide.html as the front door, or README.md with layout: plain showing a short overview plus one embedded specimen per topic (iframe) linking to the full topic page.
2. Split guide.html chapters into specimens/<topic>.html; each topic .md embeds its specimen at the top (fixed-height iframe; Flowershow allows iframes); guide.html = all specimens from the same files (single source, no drift). Don't load components.css into Flowershow pages (generic class names clash).
3. Move maintainer notes (publishing, build scripts, history) out of README into MAINTAINING.md.
4. Trim the sidebar (config.json showSidebar false, or sidebar.paths to the topic pages only); keep the navbar.
5. Optional: custom.css mapping Flowershow theme to tokens (paper ground, Polyamine headings, Bricolage body). Fetch Flowershow docs (config-file.md, custom-styles.md) before guessing options.
Read first: projects/sor-design-system/README.md, BUILD.md, guide.html, config.json, system/build-site.py. Publish: python3 system/build-site.py && fl --yes site (from projects/sor-design-system). Commit and push at end.

title: Type system for SoR experiences: pick display/body/eyebrow faces
description:
Frame 2 of 02-dawn is the test case. Current state: Polyamine (display, commercial, local() only so everyone actually sees Italiana), Crimson Text (body, disliked), Cinzel Decorative (Book illuminated letters only), accidental system-ui for meta.

Decisions taken this session:
- Keep Dawn on black (inverting kills the ember->daylight dawn mechanic).
- Drop bold AND italic from body. One weight only.
- Body face must survive both grounds (Dawn/Book black, Arrival/Flight white) since the series is half-and-half either way.
- Single-font plan (Polyamine for display+body) is dead. Two/three-face system.
- Consistent system, variable voice: one body face across whole series; display may vary per experience.
- Serif is NOT locked. Sans body wanted. Mono possible for eyebrows.
- User has no reference points to work from, so approach is react-to-reject: show complete combos, harvest dislikes.

Reference combo user liked: Fraunces (display) / Newsreader (body) / Karla (meta).

Deliverable: interactive comparator artifact with real Dawn copy, black/white ground toggle, live weight/size/leading, showing ~8 complete combos including off-beaten-path open fonts.
notes:
Heading face first, body after it is settled (user reordered; my body-first argument was right long-term but wrong as a sequence).

DELIVERABLE v3: https://claude.ai/artifact/V3NjX27AqKMjKeiwxLSfgR
Seven pre-rendered frame-2 blocks, ranked, no controls. Body held constant (Newsreader) so the heading is the only variable. Dark page throughout on purpose: white chrome between black samples wrecks eye adaptation. Nothing on disk in the repo; generated from a scratchpad script.

Ranking: 01 Bluu Next (recommended) / 02 Bagnard / 03 Cinzel / 04 Fraunces / 05 Instrument Serif / 06 Polyamine / 07 Italiana (what ships today).

RECOMMENDATION: move display from the Didone family (Polyamine, Italiana) to an inscriptional one. Argument is FIT not legibility — user confirmed headings read fine as-is, so stroke thinning is a body problem only. Tracked-out caps with no lowercase is what carved letterforms were cut for; a Didone is a text face pressed into display service, and reads luxury-goods rather than civilizational.

Deliberately excluded: sans display faces (pulls against dawn / illuminated book / renaissance framing — offer separately if wanted), heavy and condensed faces (brief asks for light widely spaced caps).

SUPERSEDED: the interactive comparator (33 fonts, sliders, ground toggle) was deleted, files and all. User: overwhelmed by choice, reinventing the wheel, wanted judgment + pre-rendered options to scroll. Lesson worth keeping: for a taste decision, ship a ranked view with reasons, not a configurator.

Two bugs found and fixed while building, both silent: (1) font stacks containing double quotes terminated the style="..." attribute, so all seven blocks fell back to the body font and rendered identically; (2) non-ASCII dashes mojibake'd without a charset — now entity-encoded.

COMMITTED: e16b3a4 docs(sor-experiences): drop bold and italic from body type (common.md + brief.md). Not pushed.
UNTRACKED, left alone deliberately: experiences/02-dawn/build/ — pre-existing, never committed; its Google Fonts link still requests Crimson 600/700/italic which are no longer needed.

NEXT: user reacts to the seven. Then body pass against the chosen heading.
STILL OPEN: experience-only type system, or shared with the main website.

--- v4: light page, full-bleed samples ---
Chrome is now light (#fbfaf7) with the seven samples as full-bleed black bands at clamp(480px,86vh,940px) — the width and height the section has live, so they read as real sections rather than cards. Commentary sits in a 1100px column between them; each band carries a discreet corner tag (rank + face name) because the label scrolls out of view inside a tall full-width band.
Chrome is theme-aware (light default, dark redefinition); the sample bands stay #080707 either way since that is content.
Verified: full bleed = viewport width, no horizontal overflow at desktop or 375px.
Reversed my earlier dark-page reasoning at user's request — eye adaptation costs a little, realism gains more.

--- v5: chrome recedes ---
All page chrome moved to the reader's own system UI sans (-apple-system/Segoe UI/Roboto), nothing loaded. Heading dropped from a 3rem display line to 1.75rem semibold; commentary muted; flag pills plain outline except the recommendation, which keeps the accent.
Real reason beyond 'quieter': the chrome was previewing the candidates. h1 was set in Bluu Next and the commentary in Newsreader, so a serif was prejudicing the comparison before the reader saw a sample. The only serifs on the page are now inside the black bands.
Newsreader remains for .ftext/.finvite inside the samples — that is the held-constant body face, correct.
NOTE: artifact sharing changed to 'anyone with the link' during this session (user did that, not me).

--- v6: weirder group ---
Feedback: the seven lack soul, too classical; Polyamine was interesting because a bit weird; they also like RESTORA.
KEY INSIGHT: Restora is by Nasir Udin — old-style roman with swashes, stylistic alternates, deliberately imperfect letterforms. Polyamine is a high-contrast display serif with quirks. Both are independent/marketplace tier, NOT institutional classics. So the taste is idiosyncratic display serifs. Cinzel and Italiana were the opposite axis — my inscriptional argument was well reasoned and aimed at the wrong target.

TECHNICAL UNLOCK: the Artifact CSP blocks the BROWSER loading fonts from other hosts, but not me downloading a file at build time and base64-embedding it. So anything downloadable can be rendered — Velvetyne (GitLab), Collletttivo (GitHub), any foundry with a free download. Velvetyne repo file paths via GitLab API; note default branch varies (master vs main).

Added, rendered: Coconat Bold (Collletttivo, NEW TOP PICK — same instinct as Polyamine, drawn better, free), Basteleur Moonlight (Velvetyne, Tarot de Marseille, medieval x Cooper Black — the one with soul), Cantique (Velvetyne, art-nouveau, far end), Flor de Ruina / Ruina (Velvetyne, decayed wood type).
Evaluated and CUT after looking: Fungal (mycelial growth only affects lowercase, capitals get nothing), Imago Mundi Mei (pictogram font), Mourier (past legibility), Amdal (not weird), Flor de Ruina Fractura (diamond between every word), Ouroboros (reads 70s psychedelic), Coconat Regular (only eccentric at heavier weights).
Lesson: build a contact sheet and LOOK before recommending. Half the shortlist was unusable for reasons no description would reveal.

Group three added: commercial faces to look up, not embeddable — Restora/Restora Neue, Signifier (Klim), GT Sectra (Grilli), Ogg (Sharp), Reckless (Displaay), Swear Display (OH no), Migra (Pangram Pangram), Cardinal Fruit (Blaze), plus Future Fonts / UNCUT / Velvetyne / Collletttivo as catalogues.

RANKING NOW: Coconat Bold > Basteleur Moonlight > Bluu Next (best of classical if pulling back). Cantique and Flor de Ruina are the far end.
OPEN: the brief's 'light, widely spaced capitals' came from Polyamine — worth deciding if it is a real requirement or an artefact of the starting face.

--- ROUND ONE REVIEWED (2026-09-30) ---
LIKED: Polyamine, Restora (Nasir Udin). Everything else rejected.
Archived at projects/2026-sor-experiences/type/round-01-headings.html, committed 8fdc10c, with each verdict in close to the client's own words. build-round-01.py regenerates it; fonts/ is a gitignored download cache.

THE TWO RULES THAT EXPLAIN THE REJECTIONS:
1. 'Boring, no personality' — killed Bluu Next, Instrument Serif, Italiana, Fraunces, Reckless, Signifier.
2. 'Backward-looking, going backwards rather than forwards' — killed Basteleur (runes/Nordic), Cinzel, Bagnard. This is a NEW renaissance emerging forward, not a return to the last one, so historical revival is out even when well drawn. Least obvious rule, explains the most.
Also: Cantique = woo-woo/new-age. Coconat Bold = fat, heavy, not elegant. GT Sectra = too sharp, 'feels like you're going to be cut'. Ogg = newspaper. Migra = barber shop or pub. Flor de Ruina = video game / disco ball. Definite no.
EXCEPTION WORTH KEEPING: Signifier rejected as heading but 'could be used for body text' — live body candidate.

CONTRAST PRINCIPLE (client's own words): 'if you take that [sleek luxurious display] you have to compensate with something more weighty and grounded in the body.' So body must CONTRAST, not match. Neutral is not grounded — a quiet workhorse would leave no ballast anywhere. This is the body brief.

ROLE SPLIT — now five roles, four faces:
- Billboard (heroes, experience pages, used sparingly) = Polyamine. Ships NO weight range, so billboard-only by necessity.
- Heading (ordinary headings, web now + print later) = Restora. Eight weights thin-black with italics, so it runs a hierarchy.
- Body = OPEN, being researched.
- Eyebrow/meta = OPEN, being researched.
- Subheading = NOT a face. Size and weight within the heading family.
Billboard and heading rarely share a page, so they need to belong to the same world, not the same family — which defuses the usual objection to two display faces.

IMPORTANT UNTESTED ASSUMPTION: everything in round one was judged as a BILLBOARD — one line at ~45px on black. Nothing has been seen at working heading size among body copy. 'Restora is more readable' is a hypothesis, not an observation; swashes and imperfect letterforms can read busier at 24px than at 45px.

BUDGET: purchases are fine, price not a constraint.
IN FLIGHT: two Sonnet subagents researching body faces and eyebrow/meta faces against the distilled brief.

--- ROUND TWO BUILT (body + eyebrow) ---
Artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/Gr3K5DYxpoB6hP4XZ1nR9L
Repo: projects/2026-sor-experiences/type/round-02-body.html, build-round-02.py. Committed f05a068.

METHOD: one variable per block. Body section holds eyebrow at Apfel Grotezk; eyebrow section holds body at Bespoke Slab. Statement set in Polyamine standing in for Restora (commercial, cannot embed) so it renders only where Polyamine is installed.

BODY RANKING (mine, after rendering all 7 on both grounds myself):
B1 Bespoke Slab - PICK. Most genuinely weighty without being fat. Low contrast, holds colour on black, contemporary not Victorian.
B2 Bespoke Serif - same family minus slabs. More elegant, less heft.
B3 Bricolage Grotesque - the sans. Strongest contrast, ink traps mark it as drawn now not revived.
B4 Hoover - most personality, narrow and mannered, may tire over length.
B5 Sentient - INCLUDED AS A FAILURE MODE. Elegant but sits in the display register, so it is a smaller cousin of the heading rather than a counterweight. Demoted from the agent's #3 for exactly this.
B6 Literata - the safe baseline, expect 'boring'.
Dropped after looking: Recia (conventional, boring risk).

EYEBROW: Apfel Grotezk (pick) / Azeret Mono (texture option) / Ysabeau Office (warm option).
Cut from the agent's list before showing: Fraunces (user already rejected it outright), Spectral SC (agent's own risk note was 'newspaper', which killed Ogg), Familjen Grotesk and Amulya (polite/friendly-UI, boring risk).

PRACTICAL FINDING: the invitation line ends in a down arrow and several otherwise good faces have NO arrow glyph. Verified by parsing cmap tables with fontTools in a venv (system python is externally managed, needs a venv). All three shown carry both arrow and middot. Apfel = 339 glyphs.

COMMERCIAL NOT SHOWN (cannot embed): Arizona Mix (Dinamo) and Right Serif (Pangram Pangram) were the agent's strongest paid picks. Signifier only passes at 500, not 400, and sits near the 'too cutty' complaint that killed GT Sectra.

NEXT: user reacts to round two. Then the untested question - does Restora hold at working heading size among body copy.

--- ROUND TWO REVIEWED ---
BODY CHOSEN: 1. Bricolage Grotesque, 2. Bespoke Serif (against Polyamine). Out: Bespoke Slab, Hoover, Sentient, Literata.
Page reworked, committed 9588d40: chosen two at top with full frames, rejected four in a collapsed <details> at the foot (kept, not deleted, so later rounds don't re-propose them), eyebrow section in the middle and now held against Bricolage rather than the rejected Bespoke Slab.

THE LESSON, WHICH CONTRADICTS MY RECOMMENDATION: I picked Bespoke Slab. It lost, and so did every serif except one. A SANS came first. So the wanted contrast between display and body is a CHANGE OF KIND, NOT OF DEGREE — not more weight inside the same family of shapes, but a different skeleton. Ink traps and contemporary grotesque construction also pass the 'not backward-looking' test in a way a well-drawn low-contrast serif does not.
Consequence: the paid options still worth trialling (Arizona Mix / Dinamo, Right Serif / Pangram Pangram) are the right ones, because both sit nearer Bricolage than the serifs.

STILL OPEN: eyebrow (Apfel Grotezk / Azeret Mono / Ysabeau Office, no feedback yet). And the untested question — does Restora hold at working heading size among body copy, as opposed to billboard size.

--- CLOSED ---
FINAL: Billboard = Polyamine. Heading = Restora. Body = Bricolage Grotesque. Eyebrow/meta = Apfel Grotezk.
Application rules (provisional, to be tested against real layouts in the design-system session): Polyamine has NO weight range so it only works large — 5-10 words at a size, not for pull quotes, not for small headings. In an ordinary article it is the hero and nothing else; H1-H4 in running text are Restora. Subheads are Restora at another size, not a fifth face.

Written up: projects/2026-sor-experiences/type.md (decisions + patterning), type/research-notes.md (working, rejections with the exact words, sources, verified download URLs, technique, method lessons). common.md and README repointed. Commits 8fdc10c, f05a068, 9588d40, c431cc9.
Artifacts: round one https://claude.ai/artifact/V3NjX27AqKMjKeiwxLSfgR / round two https://claude.ai/artifact/Gr3K5DYxpoB6hP4XZ1nR9L

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT DONE HERE:
- Licence and self-host Polyamine and Restora (neither bought; Polyamine loads via local() so it falls back for everyone else). Overlaps design-323.9.
- Restora has never been tested at working heading size among body copy — only as a billboard line at ~45px. 'More readable' is still a hypothesis.
- Landing-page exemplars and the typographic patterning proper: deferred to the design-system session. Relates to design-lpe.9.

title: Leap: decide whether to shorten scroll track 6 to ~3 viewports
description: Open question (undecided). The Leap's scroll track is 600vh (6 viewports). Concern: scroll-driven frames make visitors scroll a long way before reaching later content; with several scroll frames the page total gets long. Options: (a) keep 6; (b) tighten to ~3 viewports (main proposal); (c) hybrid: scroll triggers each beat but beats play on time; (d) time-played on entry. Related: keep total scroll budget across home page sane (~8-10 viewports before content), always-visible skip/join path, deep links bypass animation. Decide by feel + quick phone test with ~5 people. Build: projects/sor-experiences-2026/experiences/03-leap/build/index.html (.x-leap__track height, timing in render/words).
